newsitem.title: USA: Tourists said held in Turkey for aiding Kurds.
newsitem.headline: Tourists said held in Turkey for aiding Kurds.

text.p: A Polish-American man, a Polish woman and an Iranian man were abducted by Kurdish guerrillas in Turkey last month, then arrested by Turkish authorities following their release, the State Department said on Thursday.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns said guerrillas of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) abducted the three tourists from a local bus in eastern Turkey on Sept. 23.

Following their release by the PKK, the three were taken into custody by Turkish authorities in the town of Bingol on Sept. 27 on charges of rendering assistance to a terrorist organisation, Burns told reporters.
He said U.S. officials learned two days later that one of the three, originally described as a Pole, also held American citizenship. Burns named him as Christopher Mrozowski.
Polish television, in a report on Tuesday monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, named the woman involved as Magdalena Glowacka. The name of the Iranian was not available.
Burns said officials from the U.S. consulate in Adana had been able to visit Mrozowski on Tuesday and Wednesday.
He said the case was currently under investigation and awaiting trial, but that if convicted the three faced sentences ranging from three years, nine months to 10 years.
Thousands of people have died over the past decade in fighting between Turkish forces and the separatist PKK.
